reasons.A: Block-carrier: a wooden carrying yoke across the shoulders, the strongest outline of the run and unmistakable from the ARPG camera, over a dust-masked, hand-wrapped quarryman (second critic 7.5, first; first critic 6.15, fourth).
reasons.D: Charnel warden: a dark slate box helm over a pale, heavy body with a skull charm at the hip, the run's only funerary touch and its best fit on both bodies (7.2, second; first critic 4.6, sixth).
reasons.B: Dust-capped quarryman: the most dust-white set of the run, crossed straps under a strong slate cap that reads from above (6.55, third; first critic 5.9, fifth).

fixes.A: The body is iron-grey: warm it to dust white, hang clear loads (stone blocks, tools) from the yoke ends, and add one funerary sign.
fixes.D: Shape the box helm as a burial niche, whiten the body away from iron, and make one tool big enough to read.
fixes.B: A pale strapped box risks reading as linen: a colder white with rusted iron, a bigger cap or hood, and one big tool.

notes: 5 of 6 survived the draft; g00 hit its 70-turn cap without a manifest and passed after one resume (40 turns), so 6 of 6 went to the critics, and 6 of 6 survived the rework. The two critics disagreed more than in any other Grashan run: pass 1 put F (stone-block mask, rust mantle) and E first, but after the rework both read as iron and fell to the bottom, while A took first with the shoulder yoke the first critic asked for (the draft's 'Yoke' had none that read): the one rework in this wave that clearly raised a set. Every set's pale grey body leans toward iron; the funerary half of the brief and readable tools are mostly missing.
